Range Boundary Validation: Tare, Weight, Dimensions & GPS

10 min read Updated: November 2026 By Rajvardhan Singh Rathore
Physical transport equipment is constrained by physical laws and legal highway weight limits. Discover how to build domain-aware range validation rules for freight weights, volumes, and GPS boundaries.

Physical Transport Equipment Limits

Transportation data validation rules should enforce physical and regulatory reality:

  • Standard Parcel: Weight between 0.05 kg and 70.0 kg; max length ≤ 274 cm.
  • 20ft ISO Shipping Container: Max gross mass = 30,480 kg; tare weight ≈ 2,200 kg.
  • 40ft High Cube Container: Max gross mass = 32,500 kg; tare weight ≈ 3,800 kg.
  • Semi-Trailer Highway Limit: Max gross vehicle weight 36,287 kg (80,000 lbs US federal limit).

Database CHECK Constraints on DDL

PostgreSQL DDL CHECK Constraints 
ALTER TABLE master_shipments
  ADD CONSTRAINT chk_weight_positive CHECK (declared_weight_kg > 0.01 AND declared_weight_kg <= 45000.00),
  ADD CONSTRAINT chk_packages_count CHECK (total_packages >= 1 AND total_packages <= 10000),
  ADD CONSTRAINT chk_valid_lat CHECK (origin_lat >= -90.0 AND origin_lat <= 90.0),
  ADD CONSTRAINT chk_valid_lon CHECK (origin_lon >= -180.0 AND origin_lon <= 180.0);

GPS Coordinate Bounding Box Filtering

If a regional linehaul operates solely within continental North America, GPS coordinates falling outside the bounding box (Lat: 24.5° to 49.4°N, Lon: 66.9° to 124.8°W) are immediately isolated as sensor errors.

Cargo Density Anomaly Detection

Calculate cargo density ($ ext{Density} = rac{ ext{Weight (kg)}}{ ext{Volume} (m^3)}$). Liquid petroleum or iron ore has high density (~1000 - 7000 kg/m³); foam pillows have low density (~15 kg/m³). Records deviating from established commodity density ranges by > 3 standard deviations are flagged for re-weigh inspection.
